title: KV workload fingerprinting & regression detector — hit-rate vs latency vs memory
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Objective: build a reproducible benchmarking harness that fingerprints KV/prefix-cache workloads and detects regressions across hit-rate, latency (p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), and memory (RSS / cache footprint). The harness must support both synthetic workload generation and replay of anonymized production traces, sweep cache sizing and prefetching policies, and provide a deterministic baseline for automated PR checks and CI gating.
test_plan: Implement workload fingerprinting: collect distribution of prefix lengths, token sequence lengths, concurrency histogram, and prefix reuse patterns from anonymized traces.
Create a synthetic workload generator that can reshape traces to target hit-rates (10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%) while preserving sequence length and concurrency distributions.
Sweep cache footprint (1GB, 2GB, 4GB, 8GB, 16GB) and observe hit-rate, eviction rate, and memory RSS.
Measure latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, and CPU/GPU utilization for each sweep point using the same model binaries used in production (rw-optimized-13b, rw-optimized-7b).
Run each configuration for at least 30 minutes steady-state to capture tail behavior and warm/cold start effects; repeat 5 times to compute confidence intervals.
Integrate regression detection into CI: baseline snapshot per release and PR-run comparisons with automatic pass/fail rules and Slack alerts for infra owners.
Store serialized results to perf-bench DB and link to perf dashboard showing trends and heatmaps (hit-rate vs p95 vs cache_size).
measurement_matrix: Primary metrics: p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec, KV hit-rate (%), cache RSS (GB)
Secondary metrics: p50, p99, eviction/sec, prefetched_keys/sec, CPU and GPU utilization, GC cycles, tail-event rate (>2x p95)
Derived metrics: tokens/sec per GB, p95 per 1% hit-rate improvement, cost-estimated token cost delta
instrumentation: Expose per-request KV lookup timing (ns), hit/miss flag, and per-eviction cost in trace logs
Emit aggregated 10s windows: hit-rate, eviction/sec, avg lookup latency, p95/p99 latency
Add stable run-id and seed in harness to ensure reproducible synthetic workloads
Collect system RSS and cgroup memory pressure metrics alongside process-level counters
Add x-ray traces linking request tokens -> KV lookups -> model forward timing for tail debugging
regression_detection: Baseline: take a release snapshot baseline for each major model/runtime combo (weekly runs).
Statistical checks: bootstrap CI on p95 and tokens/sec; require 95% CI overlap to pass, otherwise flag.
Heuristics: auto-fail if p95 increases by >10% AND tokens/sec drops by >5% relative to baseline for same config.
CUSUM + consecutive-failure detection to prevent flapping on noisy metrics; require 3 consecutive PR runs failing to auto-open a Sev ticket.
Annotate PRs touching cache, prefetch, or kernel selection with a required perf-check job that runs a minimal suite (fast mode) and attaches results to the PR.
Provide a manual override path for known noisy configs with an explanatory link and owner sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can reproduce existing baseline numbers within ±5% for p95 and tokens/sec on repeat runs.
Workload fingerprinting produces a compact fingerprint JSON that can be used to synthesize an equivalent load.
CI integration: PRs touching cache logic run the perf-check job and surface a pass/fail result in the PR status.
Dashboard: heatmap view of hit-rate vs p95 vs cache_size available, and historical baselines for at least 4 weeks.
Regression detector opens an automated issue when thresholds are crossed and not acknowledged within 24 hours.
initial_results_summary: Initial runs (2026-03-01) on anonymized trace 'prod-trace-2026-02-sample' show: with cache_size=8GB and prefix dedupe enabled, measured KV hit-rate=72% resulting in tokens/sec +9% and p95 latency -12ms compared to no-cache baseline. A prefetching prototype improved tokens/sec at low concurrency but increased p95 by ~60ms under 500 concurrent streams due to a single prefetch worker contention. These findings suggest prefetch concurrency control is required.
actions_next_steps: Split prefetch pipeline into N workers with backpressure and retry delays; prototype initial fix ENG-30568 assigned to Ravi.
Add synthetic workload generator knob to replay exact per-request key sequences (not just distributions) for worst-case tail repros.
Wire the CI perf-check job to create a historical artifact and link to perf-dashboard automatically.
Schedule cross-team review with SRE (Linus Gordon) and Product (Maya Chen) on 2026-03-12 to agree on regression thresholds and alerting policy.
